summary: Iteration 12 retest of the iteration 11 fixes. Backend: test_iter11_edge.py + test_iter11_maintenance.py pass 12/12 with -n 0, so the history fix works (a service job finished after reminders were stopped still logs cost + contractor). New tests/test_iter12_retest.py passes 1 of 3. /api/properties palette is 0,1,2 (pass), but /api/onboarding?property_id= gives palette 0 for all 3 demo rentals. Frontend (375x667, test_ui11) verified: Rentals cover art has 3 different colours (#FBE3DA / #E5EBD8 / #DCE8EC); Bench chip avatars match; cover button offsetHeight is 44px; 'Load demo' / 'Reset demo' not truncated; appliance card caption reads 'Next service · every year'; 'Book a pro' / 'Edit' not truncated; ScheduleSheet with last_done 2026-10-25 moves due text to Apr 25 2027 (6), Jan 25 2027 (3) and Oct 25 2027 (12); Fix-it subtitle reads 'Every year · Garage · Oct 30'; issue title is 'Rheem water heater service at Tahoe Cabin' from both Fix-it and the appliance screen, with the Routine service badge; Fix-it Mark done -> toast Undo -> card comes back. One fix NOT working: the /appliances?pid= cover is terracotta (palette 0) for all 3 rentals, so Joshua Tree and Oakland don't match their Rentals card colour. No console errors. test_ui11 restored: water heater yearly, due 2026-10-30, no logs, no jobs, no covers.

minor.issue: palette is count_documents(created_at < prop.created_at). seed.py:103 gives every demo rental the same created_at (now), so all 3 demo rentals get palette 0. Reproduced by tests/test_iter12_retest.py::test_onboarding_palette_matches and ::test_created_at_unique (all 3 created_at = 2026-10-25T06:28:24.995). Also, /properties and host_catalog sort only by created_at, so with tied timestamps the order (and so the colour) isn't guaranteed to stay the same.

ui_bugs.issue: The house drawing uses palette 0 (terracotta #FBE3DA) for every rental, so Joshua Tree (sage) and Oakland (lake) don't match their Rentals card or Bench chip. Cause: the backend palette bug above.

action_items: Fix the palette for /onboarding (used by /appliances?pid=): work out the index the same way /properties does. For example, add a shared helper that fetches the host's rentals sorted by [('created_at',1),('id',1)] and returns the rental's index. Use that same sort in list_properties and host_catalog so tied timestamps always give the same order.

In seed.py, give the demo rentals different created_at values (e.g. now - timedelta(seconds=len(props)-i)) so the order is clear. Existing hosts already have tied timestamps, so the helper fix is still needed.
Re-run tests/test_iter12_retest.py (the created_at uniqueness test only passes after a demo reset once the seed is fixed. It's informational, the palette match test is the key one).
critical_code_review_comments: onboarding_routes.state palette uses count_documents with $lt created_at, which breaks on tied timestamps and doesn't match the enumerate() index used in server.py. Two different ways of working out the same value.
